## Functional requirements

| ID | Requirement | Verify |
|----|-------------|--------|
| REQ-F-001 | The app shall resolve a user-selected instrument symbol to its eToro instrument id and only enable trading once the resolution is confirmed. | T |
| REQ-F-002 | The app shall poll live prices for the selected instrument and display them in a chart and price read-out. The chart's price-axis labels and its current-price tag shall carry at least three decimals and shall follow the magnitude of the instrument on screen (more for a low-priced one such as a forex pair), so a label is never rounded to a price the instrument never had. | T |
| REQ-F-003 | The app shall place market orders with a configurable cash amount, leverage, stop-loss and take-profit (entered as account-currency amounts), guarded by a deliberate double-press confirmation. | T |
| REQ-F-004 | The app shall reject orders that would exceed a configured total open-exposure cap, and enforce a cooldown between consecutive orders. | T |
| REQ-F-005 | The app shall compute the classic technical indicators (SMA, EMA, RSI, stochastic %K, MACD histogram, Bollinger %B, volatility, ROC, mean return) as pure functions over a close-price series. | T |
| REQ-F-006 | The app shall provide statistical forecasts: OLS regression (slope, R²), k-nearest-neighbour analog forecast, Hurst exponent, and a bootstrap Monte-Carlo outlook reporting P(up), a 5–95% range, and the probabilities that a long/short hits take-profit before stop-loss and vice versa. | T |
| REQ-F-007 | The app shall combine the indicators into a directional ensemble (BUY / SELL / NEUTRAL with a confidence), and trim the confidence in high-VIX and imminent-event conditions. | T |
| REQ-F-008 | The app shall blend the available per-instrument sources (technical ensemble, TradingView rating, news sentiment, market regime, crowd sentiment) into a weighted composite call per instrument, renormalising weights over available sources, and rank instruments by confidence. | T |
| REQ-F-009 | The app shall obtain crowd sentiment (CNN Fear & Greed, 0–100) and tilt the composite with it: mildly with the crowd for ordinary readings, contrarian at extremes (≤20, ≥80). | T |
| REQ-F-010 | The app shall build a costed trade plan per instrument: a BUY/SELL/STAY-OUT verdict with reason, Monte-Carlo win/lose probabilities against the proposed barriers, a break-even comparison, a 1–5 risk factor with reasons, and a volatility-targeted leverage recommendation that keeps the loss-at-stop within 25% of the stake, stepped to the instrument''s allowed leverage values and cap. The expected value shall price paths that reach neither barrier at their Monte-Carlo measured mean final move (not a flat-expiry approximation). A BUY/SELL verdict additionally requires ALL of: (a) ensemble confidence of at least 20% after the VIX and event-risk trims, (b) a Monte-Carlo win rate that clears the break-even rate by at least two standard errors of its own estimate (sampling-noise band), and (c) an expected net edge after costs of at least 0.25% of the stake; otherwise the verdict is STAY OUT with the failing gate as the reason. | T |
| REQ-F-011 | The trade plan's cost bill shall account for half the spread on opening and half on closing, the per-night rollover fee, and the one-off ~3× weekend rollover whenever the holding window includes Friday–Sunday; the expected edge shall be reported net of these costs. | T |
| REQ-F-012 | The trade panel shall default the invest amount to 3750 (display currency) and auto-propose SL/TP from recent volatility (stop ≈ 1.5σ of the horizon move, TP = 1.5 × SL) until the user edits them; an instrument switch re-enables the automatics. The automatic proposal shall never overwrite a stop-loss or take-profit field while it is being edited (keyboard focus inside the field). The same protection applies to the SL/TP cells of the open-trades table: while a cell editor is open, portfolio polls, FX updates and re-prices shall not overwrite that cell's editor; the withheld refresh is applied once editing ends. | T/I |
| REQ-F-013 | The app shall propose (never execute) closing an open position when the live price leaves the prediction corridor against it or the ensemble flips against it with ≥60% confidence, with a per-position log cooldown. | T |
| REQ-F-014 | The app shall list closed trades over a selectable 7–13-week lookback — reachable both from the closed-trades panel and from a button in the main header, and restricted by default to the instruments the app itself trades (with an explicit opt-out that lists the whole account, foreign rows greyed) — with the API's net P/L and rollover fees plus estimated open/close spread costs (half current spread × notional per side) and the spread percentage each estimate priced with, flagging spreads captured while the market was closed (frozen quotes overstate costs); it shall summarise per instrument with a Costs column = spread costs + fees and show the total costs across listed instruments next to the net P/L headline. | T |
| REQ-F-015 | The app shall infer per-instrument market-open state from whether the instrument's quote timestamp ADVANCES between successive polls — the public rates feed lags real time by minutes, so an absolute quote age must not decide it — and block MARKET orders on closed markets. Where no previous timestamp is known yet (first poll after start), a quote age generous enough to absorb that feed delay shall stand in until the next poll supplies a baseline. Limit orders (REQ-F-027) are exempt from the block: the broker parks them until its market opens, which is the normal way to be positioned for the next session. | T |
| REQ-F-016 | The app shall display account figures in EUR using the live EUR/USD rate and convert user inputs back to the account currency for the API. | T |
| REQ-F-017 | Without API credentials the app shall run fully functional against a self-contained simulation (synthetic feed, virtual account, closed-trade log). | T |
| REQ-F-018 | Configuration shall be layered: built-in defaults ← config.json (non-secret) ← apiKeyEtoro.json (secrets, git-ignored) ← environment variables. | T |
| REQ-F-019 | The app shall display an independent web reference quote (Yahoo Finance) for the selected instrument with its exchange timestamp and the delta versus the eToro rate. | T |
| REQ-F-020 | The app shall obtain market context from public feeds: CBOE VIX, TradingView technical ratings, per-instrument news headlines, and a macro-economic calendar with per-event impact heuristics. | T |
| REQ-F-021 | The decision window shall explain its conclusions in place: the trade-plan verdict carries a mouse-over stating what the verdict means and why it was reached (incl. the STAY OUT reason), the "expected edge after costs" figure carries a mouse-over defining it with the plan''s own numbers, each ranked-list call carries a mouse-over with its source breakdown, a Trade-plan column shows every ranked instrument''s own plan verdict (BUY/SELL/STAY OUT, computed off the GUI thread with the same cost and break-even gates as the trade-plan panel), a Web signal column shows every ranked instrument''s TradingView multi-timeframe technical rating (the same read that feeds the composite; eToro thematic baskets use the closest liquid ETF/index proxy, n/a where none exists), and an Open column shows each instrument''s live market-open state from the quote-freshness poll. | I |
| REQ-F-022 | The app shall obtain an independent Yahoo Finance intraday close series (1-minute session bars) per instrument and blend a session-momentum tilt derived from it into the weighted composite call, renormalised with the other sources and shown in the decision window's sources table. | T |
| REQ-F-023 | For each upcoming calendar event the app shall propose an advisory-only activity: the side (BUY/SELL, from the event class and the forecast-vs-previous change) and the timing — after the print for high-impact events (gap/whipsaw risk), before the release for lower-impact consensus — or STAY OUT with the reason when no direction can be derived. Proposals are never executed automatically. | T |
| REQ-F-024 | Clicking the Side cell of an open-trade row shall open a non-modal gauge window for that trade: a dial whose needle is the live price over a stop-loss→open→take-profit scale (loss zone red, win zone green, open-rate marker), plus the buy (open) value, the current value, the live P/L and the SL/TP values; the gauge follows live price ticks of the shown instrument. Clicking the Instrument cell shall instead switch the app to that trade''s instrument (as if picked from the instrument selector); clicks on other cells shall neither open the gauge nor switch the instrument. | I |
| REQ-F-025 | The open-trades view shall take its position set from the account's live portfolio view, never from cached P/L snapshots, so that a position closed outside the app (in eToro's own UI, or automatically by SL/TP) disappears on the next refresh. Every open trade's P/L shall be marked the way eToro marks it — units × (close rate − open rate) × the instrument's conversion rate, at the bid for a long and the ask for a short — from a quote of the current poll tick for the trade's OWN instrument, not only for the instrument on screen. A quote shall mark a position only while eToro's own timestamp for that price is younger than ~2 minutes: where eToro publishes an instrument's rate behind real time (measured at 6–12 minutes on the .24-7 index variants, and inherited by its /pnl figures), the mark shall come from that instrument's live 1-minute candle close instead, and where no current price exists at all the view shall show eToro's last snapshot figure flagged as not live rather than a figure derived from a stale price. The view shall summarise the open book below the table: the total invested amount — summing the Amount column exactly as it is shown, so the column adds up to the total — and the total P/L, restated on every re-price rather than only per poll, and flagged as not live when any row lacks a current quote. The P/L cell's tooltip shall name the rate its figure is marked at, and the stop-loss and take-profit cells — which show what each leg is worth — shall carry a tooltip naming the instrument RATE that triggers it, its distance from the open rate and from the rate the trade would close at now, the amount the cell states, and whether the stop trails; a leg that is off shall say so rather than read as a trigger at zero. When a position disappears from the portfolio, the app shall refresh the closed-trades list immediately — at most one history walk per 5 s, and the delayed refresh stays armed because the broker's trade history lags the portfolio. | T |
| REQ-F-026 | While the market-open inference reports the selected instrument closed, the app shall offer an explicit "Trade anyway" override that re-enables BUY/SELL, so a wrong closed verdict can never lock the user out of a market that is in fact open. Arming and clearing the override shall be logged, every order placed through it shall be logged as overridden, the double-press confirmation gate shall stay in force, and the override shall clear itself on an instrument switch so it can never carry over to another market. | I |
| REQ-F-027 | A conditional entry — "open this trade when the rate reaches X" — shall be placed AT THE BROKER as an eToro limit order (public-API orderType "mit" with a triggerRate), never executed by an in-app price watch: eToro triggers it off its own feed and with the app closed, whereas the app's polled quotes lag the market by minutes and stop entirely when it exits. The order shall carry the trade panel's size, leverage and SL/TP, with the SL/TP amounts converted to rates off the TRIGGER rate (where the position will open), not off the current quote. The app shall list the ACCOUNT's resting limit orders — taken from the broker's own portfolio breakdown, not merely from what this session submitted, so orders placed earlier or in eToro's own UI are visible too — with their live broker status and each order's CURRENT instrument rate (so how far the market still has to travel is visible without switching instruments), allow cancelling one before it executes, report a fill when the broker reports one, and count resting orders against the open-exposure cap. An order on an instrument outside the app's selector shall still be listed (identified by its instrument id), because an order the app hides is an order nobody can cancel. The double-press confirmation gate applies to limit orders as well, and the market-order and limit-order gates shall be independent of one another. Because eToro fills at the trigger rate OR BETTER (lower for a buy, higher for a short), a rate already on the executable side of the market can fill at once instead of resting; the app shall say so in the log before such an order goes out rather than silently letting the user assume it will wait.<br><br>A resting order shall be adjustable from that list — trigger rate, stop-loss and take-profit amounts, entered through an editor opened from the order's row — with size, leverage and side carried over unchanged. The public API offers no update-order endpoint, so the app shall implement the change as CANCEL-then-re-place (never the reverse, which could leave two live orders for one intended trade), state in the editor that the order returns under a new id, and place the replacement on the ORDER's own instrument, whichever instrument the app happens to be showing — a limit order is priced off its trigger rate, so it needs no live quote of that instrument (a MARKET order, which must be priced from a live bid/ask, stays restricted to the instrument being traded). Clicking an order's instrument cell shall additionally switch the app to that instrument, the same gesture the open-trades table uses.<br><br>A newly placed order shall appear in the list at once, and the list and its per-order statuses shall be refreshed on a fixed 4-second cycle of their own — not on the configurable price-poll cadence — running only while at least one order rests and staying inside the lookup endpoint's shared rate budget. A refresh shall not discard the row the user has marked for cancelling or adjusting. Because an accepted order (HTTP 200 with an order id) can still be REJECTED by the broker seconds later, the app shall additionally re-read a just-placed order's status ahead of that cycle, and shall report a rejection as an error carrying eToro's own reason and error code — an order the app lists as resting must never be one the broker has already refused. | T/I |
| REQ-F-028 | The app shall load a plain-text trade script: one order per line, semicolon-separated — `<instrument>; BUY @ <trigger>` or `<instrument>; SELL @ <trigger>` followed by optional keyworded fields in any order: `FROM <yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm>` and `TO <yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm>` (the trading window), `SIGNALS` (trade only on agreement, below), `AMOUNT <stake>`, `SL <amount>`, `TP <amount>`, `TRAILING` (the stop-loss trails), and `LEV <n>`. `#` starts a comment; blank lines are ignored. Loading is all-or-nothing: any unparsable line is reported with its line number and content, and nothing from that file is accepted — a half-loaded script that silently skips lines is how money gets traded that nobody asked for.<br><br>Each entry shall be executed as a broker-side eToro limit order through the REQ-F-027 machinery — BUY enters at the trigger rate or LOWER, SELL at the trigger or HIGHER, off the broker's own feed — never by an in-app price watch. An entry's order is placed no earlier than its FROM time (immediately when absent) and cancelled at its TO time if still resting (absent TO = it rests until filled or disarmed). With the SIGNALS flag, the order is placed only while BOTH the technical ensemble and the AI advisor favour the entry's side, is cancelled if either flips while it rests, and may be re-placed if they align again inside the window; an unconfigured AI advisor counts as no recommendation, so flagged entries then never place — the panel shall say so rather than trade on half the evidence. The stop-loss, take-profit and trailing flag carry into the limit order unchanged (amounts, converted off the trigger rate per REQ-F-027). When the requested leverage is not among the instrument's offered values, the app shall use the next LOWER offered value and log the substitution; when the requested value exceeds every offered one, the highest offered value is already that next-lower choice.<br><br>Scripted execution is real, unattended trading, so the double-press gate of manual orders is replaced by an equivalent two-step commitment: LOADING a script never places anything, and execution happens only while the user has explicitly ARMED the loaded script — a separate, visible action. Disarming (or loading a different file) shall cancel every scripted order still resting. Each entry executes at most once per arming; every placement, cancellation, substitution and skip shall be logged with the entry's script line; scripted orders count against the open-exposure cap like manual ones. While a script is loaded but DISARMED, the panel shall still evaluate every entry against the live data and log what WOULD be placed — a dry run, so a script can be rehearsed before it is trusted with money. | T/I |
| REQ-F-029 | The app shall provide an autonomous trading-bot SIMULATION that trades the app's own multi-source decision engine (REQ-F-008) across ALL selectable instruments with SIMULATED money against LIVE market data, so that the question "would this strategy have made money over a longer period" can be answered without risking any. The simulated account shall start at 50 000 EUR (configurable), and the simulation shall be strictly and structurally separated from the broker: the bot shall never place, modify or cancel an order at eToro, never move real money, and never require or use write credentials — it reads quotes, spreads, fees and signals only. Because it therefore moves no money, the double-press gate of REQ-N-005 does not apply to it; it is armed by one explicit visible action instead, and while disarmed it does nothing but keep its books.<br><br>Decisions shall come from the same machinery the decision window uses — the weighted composite over the technical ensemble, TradingView rating, news sentiment, VIX/calendar regime, crowd sentiment and the independent intraday series — evaluated for EVERY instrument on each all-instruments scan: a positive composite is a simulated BUY, a negative one a simulated SELL, and the bot shall be deliberately courageous (a low confidence floor) rather than trade rarely, since the purpose is to measure the strategy's behaviour over many trades. An instrument whose market is closed, whose price is unknown or which the bot already holds shall not be entered. Position size, leverage and the stop-loss / take-profit levels shall be derived from the instrument's own recent volatility (the REQ-F-011 geometry: stop ≈ 1.5σ of the horizon, reward:risk 1.5, leverage the largest allowed value keeping the loss at stop within the per-trade risk budget), bounded by a per-trade stake fraction of the CURRENT simulated equity, a total-margin cap and a hard leverage cap.<br><br>How MANY trades the bot holds shall not be a policy number: it shall take as many as its decision source judges worthwhile, and the limit shall be a PORTFOLIO RISK BUDGET — the summed loss-if-every-stop-is-hit of all open simulated trades shall stay within a configured fraction of equity, and each new stake shall be clipped to the room that is left. A refusal for that reason shall name it as the risk budget rather than as a queue limit, because the two mean opposite things to whoever reads the log. A concurrency bound may remain only as a sanity limit far above what one-position-per-instrument can reach. Two hard invariants bound the same decision: the simulated account shall never commit more margin than a configured fraction of equity — leaving free margin, since an account with none is one a real broker margin-calls — and it shall NEVER commit money it does not hold: cash, out of which the opening costs are paid on top of the stakes, shall never go negative. Each scan shall report both limits (risk at stop against its budget, margin committed against its cap, and free cash), because either can be the one that stopped the bot and the log must not leave the reader guessing which. All computation shall stay off the GUI thread's critical path — the entry evaluation uses closed-form volatility geometry, not the Monte-Carlo path of REQ-F-010.<br><br>Simulated fills and costs shall be modelled the way the real path is charged — and each cost charged EXACTLY ONCE, so the measured result is neither flattered nor pessimistic for an invisible reason. Opening and closing shall each cost half the instrument's LIVE spread on the position's notional (REQ-F-025's identity), charged as an explicit, displayed amount; fills and marks shall therefore be priced at the quote's MID, which is economically the ask fill for a buy and the bid fill for a sell once that half-spread is paid, while keeping the transaction cost visible in the books instead of buried inside the rates. Overnight rollover shall be charged per night held from the instrument's own per-unit fees, with the weekend night charged at the tripled rate (REQ-F-013), and a negative fee shall stay a credit. P/L shall use the FX-free identity stake × leverage × (mark − open) / open signed by the side, marked from the same live quotes the real open-trades table is marked from, and a mark taken from a quote that is no longer live shall be shown as such rather than presented as a current P/L. A simulated position shall close when its stop-loss or take-profit rate is touched, when the composite decision flips against it with conviction, or when a maximum holding time expires — each closure recording its reason.<br><br>Closing shall also be an ECONOMIC decision, not only a price one, because a leveraged position pays rent every night and eToro bills the Friday night three times (REQ-F-013). Two carry rules shall therefore apply. First, when what is still to be won — the remaining distance to the take-profit on the position's notional — no longer covers what holding it to the end of the intended horizon will cost (the rollover nights in between plus the half-spread it must still cross to exit), the position shall close: a trade that cannot out-earn its own rent is a loss being paid for in instalments. Second, the TRIPLED weekend charge shall have to be earned: a position whose current net does not cover that charge shall be closed before paying it, which also sheds the weekend gap risk, while one already ahead by more than the charge may ride through. A rollover CREDIT shall never be a reason to close — being paid to hold is not a cost — and where the instrument's fee table is unknown the carry rules shall stay silent rather than guess, exactly as the entry gate refuses an unknown spread instead of pricing it at zero. A touched stop or target shall still take precedence over both.<br><br>The bot shall be able to take its proposal from a LOCAL large language model instead of (or in addition to) the composite — see REQ-F-030.<br><br>The bot's window shall show, at all times: the account line (start capital, cash, invested, equity, open P/L, realised P/L and total P/L in EUR and percent); every OPEN simulated trade with its instrument, side, invested amount, leverage, entry rate, current mark, stop-loss / take-profit, accumulated costs (spread paid to open plus rollover so far) and current P/L; every CLOSED simulated trade with its entry and exit, holding time, total costs, net P/L and WHEN and why it closed — the time of an exit belongs with its reason, since a record of exits without their times says nothing about whether the rules fired when they should; and per-decision log lines stating what the bot did and why it did it. Opening a position shall additionally raise a notice the user acknowledges, so a bot left running cannot open positions unnoticed; that notice shall NOT be modal — a modal box would stop the marking and exit evaluation, freezing the bot until someone clicked — and at most one shall be on screen at a time, because a single scan can open a dozen trades and a dozen stacked dialogs is a lockout rather than a notification. EVERY scan shall additionally log one summary line — candidates considered, trades opened, positions held, risk at stake against the budget, and a count per refusal category — because a window that says nothing while the bot decides nothing is indistinguishable from a broken bot, and the reason a scan opened nothing is exactly what the experimenter needs.<br><br>The simulated books shall survive a restart of the app, and so shall the SESSION state that decides whether the experiment is running at all: the armed flag and the decision-source mode shall be persisted and restored, with the restored state stated in the log. An experiment meant to run for days must not stop silently the first time the app is reopened — an armed bot that comes back disarmed looks exactly like a bot that is working and finding nothing. The books shall be resettable to the starting capital in one action. | T/I |
| REQ-F-030 | The app shall be able to obtain a trading proposal from a LOCAL large language model served by Ollama, and the bot simulation (REQ-F-029) shall be able to trade on it. The model shall be given the SAME evidence prompt the decision window hands the cloud advisor (REQ-F-008) — the ranked candidates with their per-source reads and the market context — and shall answer with a RANKED LIST of proposals — every instrument it considers worth trading now, best first, each with instrument, BUY / SELL / HOLD, a confidence, a leverage and a short rationale — so that the protocol never becomes the thing that limits how many trades the bot takes; that limit is the risk budget of REQ-F-029. A bounded number of picks shall be accepted from one answer, and an empty list ("nothing worth trading") shall be reported as such rather than as a failure or a HOLD. The answer shall be requested as strict JSON (Ollama's `format` field) and parsed defensively: a model that answers with prose, with JSON wrapped in commentary, or with an unknown instrument shall produce a reported failure or a HOLD, never a trade on a guess.<br><br>The endpoint and model shall be configuration, not code: an Ollama host (default http://localhost:11434) and a model name, resolvable from config.json and from the environment like every other setting (REQ-F-018), with no key required — this is a local service. The app shall be able to state whether that service is actually usable, by listing the models the daemon serves and reporting a clear diagnosis when the host is unreachable, when no model is configured, or when the configured model is not installed; a missing or unreachable Ollama shall never block the app, the bot, or any other feature.<br><br>Because a local model runs on the user's own hardware and may take tens of seconds, the request shall be asynchronous and shall never block the GUI thread, and at most one request shall be in flight at a time. A proposal shall be judged by the AGE of the reasoning behind it, not by whether a newer scan has completed meanwhile: it shall be applied to the latest candidate set while it is younger than one scan cycle — the entry it leads to is re-validated against the live quote, spread and market state of the instrument it names anyway — and shall be dropped, with the delay stated, once it is older than that. Discarding every answer that a newer scan overtook would silently disable the feature on exactly the hardware it exists for, since a slow model is regularly overtaken.<br><br>How the simulator uses the proposal shall be an explicit, visible choice with three settings: OFF (the composite decides, as in REQ-F-029), CONFIRM (only the proposal's instrument may be opened, and only while the composite agrees with the model's side — the model is a veto, not a source of direction), and LEAD (the model's own pick and side are traded). In every setting every pick shall be shown and logged with its rationale, so what the model said is on the record whether or not it was acted on, and an instrument refused because the model chose others shall say which ones. In no setting shall the model be able to bypass the risk rules: the stake fraction, the exposure and concurrency caps, the one-position-per-instrument rule, the ruin guard, the market-open and live-spread requirements and the volatility-derived stop/target geometry all continue to apply, and the leverage the model asks for shall be capped by them. The model shall never place a real order — it feeds the simulation only. | T/I |
| REQ-F-031 | The bot shall pursue a DAILY result target (default 350 EUR of booked net, configurable) under rules that make the pursuit survivable, and it shall be explicit that no strategy can guarantee a fixed daily profit: the target is a stopping rule, not a promise. Three rules follow from that. Once the day's BOOKED net reaches the target the bot shall open nothing further that day, so a made day cannot be given back; once the day's booked net reaches the loss limit it shall likewise stop opening, so a bad day cannot become a bad month; and in no circumstance shall position size be increased to recover a loss — the stake is a fraction of CURRENT equity, so it can only shrink after losses. Only realised money shall count towards either rule: open profit can still turn, and a rule reading it would stop on nothing. Because a daily goal must therefore be BOOKED, the bot shall close the SMALLEST open position whose own net result — after the exit cost — already completes the day's target, leaving larger winners running; this truncates that one position's upside, which is a deliberate, documented cost of aiming at a daily number rather than at the best possible total, and it shall be switchable. Positions already open shall continue to be governed by their own stops, targets and carry rules. Trading shall be restricted to Monday–Friday, and per instrument to the sessions the market-open inference reports (REQ-F-015). Both directions shall be traded on equal terms: a negative composite (or a model SELL) shall open a SHORT with mirrored stop/target geometry, the same sizing, the same risk per euro of stake and the sell-side rollover — and the record shall attribute result to longs and shorts separately, so an edge that exists only in a rising market cannot hide inside a total.<br><br>Risk shall be aggregated by CORRELATION, not by position count: every instrument shall belong to a bucket of things that move together (equity indices, FX, precious metals, other commodities; an unrecognised symbol gets its own bucket), the loss-at-stop of the open positions shall be summed per bucket, and no bucket shall be allowed more than a configured fraction of equity — well below the portfolio budget, so that budget cannot be spent on a single market view. Holding a dozen long index positions is one bet with one outcome; the refusal shall name the bucket rather than the portfolio budget, and the scan summary shall show where the risk actually sits.<br><br>Whether the strategy may be trusted with REAL money shall be decided by measured evidence, never by impression. The app shall compute, from the closed-trade record alone: the number of closed trades and distinct trading days, net after all costs, net per day and the rolling net of the last few days, gross wins and losses, profit factor, expectancy per trade, win rate, the deepest peak-to-trough drawdown of the closed-trade curve in EUR and as a percentage of starting capital, how often the daily target was actually reached, and the long/short split. It shall compare those figures against configurable thresholds — a minimum sample of trades AND of days, a net above zero after costs, a profit factor and an expectancy above stated minima, and a maximum tolerable drawdown — and shall report either readiness or EVERY unmet condition in plain words. The bot shall not be connectable to real-money execution while any condition is unmet, and the window shall state the verdict and its blockers at all times, so "it seems to work" is never the basis of that decision. | T/A |
| REQ-F-032 | The bot shall be able to hold MORE THAN ONE position in the same instrument, but only on the local model's own initiative: a second or further position shall require that the model named that instrument in its current answer, shall be refused beyond a configured count per instrument, and shall be refused beyond a per-instrument share of equity at risk that is tighter than the correlation-bucket cap (several positions in one symbol are the same bet, sized up). Opposite sides in one instrument shall never be held at the same time — a change of side is a close, not a hedge.<br><br>The model shall also be asked about what is ALREADY OPEN, not only about what to open next: the evidence prompt shall list the held positions with their side, age and result so far, and a position shall be closed when the model answers with the opposite side for that instrument or asks explicitly to close it. Silence shall NEVER close a position: a small local model regularly answers about a fraction of the instruments it is shown, and reading absence as "close everything" would liquidate the book on a slow answer. Every open position shall be reviewed on every pass and shall carry the model's CURRENT conclusion where the position is shown — hold, close, or "not mentioned" — with the model's own words as the explanation; "not mentioned" is a first-class state and shall never be displayed as either recommendation. With the model switched off, no such verdict shall be sought or acted on.<br><br>Exits shall further follow the trade's own DYNAMICS rather than only its fixed levels. A position whose entry signal has faded to a fraction of the conviction that opened it, and which is not in profit, shall be closed rather than ridden to its stop; a position that was up by a material amount and has handed back most of it shall be closed while it is still a winner. The best result each position has shown shall be remembered across restarts, since that is what the second rule compares against.<br><br>Costs shall be part of the ENTRY decision, not only of the exit rules: the gain if the target is reached shall be compared against the full round trip (both half-spreads plus the rollover to the horizon, weekend nights included), and a trade whose target is not worth a configured multiple of what it costs shall be refused with that reason named. | T/A |
| REQ-F-033 | Every trade the simulator closes shall be recorded as a training example: the features that were true when it was opened (conviction, volatility, stop and target distance, spread, edge-over-cost, leverage, direction, hour and weekday, and whether the model backed it) together with what the trade actually made after all costs. The record shall be an append-only file, and the label shall be the NET result — a trade that moved the right way but did not cover its costs is a loss and shall be learned as one.<br><br>A small feed-forward network shall be trainable from that record by a tool shipped with the project, and the app shall read the resulting model and score each candidate before it is taken. The model's inputs shall be matched BY NAME against the feature list it was trained on, so a model trained on a different set is detected and refused rather than read one column out of step. Validation shall use the LATEST trades in the record, never a random sample, and the measured quality shall be stored with the model.<br><br>The network shall have to EARN the right to refuse: below a configured number of training examples, or below a configured out-of-sample quality, it shall be scored and reported but shall never block a trade, and it shall never be able to open one. Its influence shall be configurable between off, advisory and gating, and the window shall state which of those applies together with what the model measured. | T/A |
| REQ-F-034 | Trading frequency shall be governed, because every round trip pays two half-spreads and, held overnight, rent: a measured hour of the simulation produced six closes with a median holding time of 5.2 minutes, 1.64 EUR of gross profit and 19.38 EUR of costs — the strategy did not lose that money, the churn did. Three rules shall follow. An instrument whose position has just closed shall not be re-entered for a configured cooldown; the book as a whole shall open no more than a configured number of positions per hour; and no position shall be closed by OPINION — a model changing its mind, a faded signal, a surrendered gain — before it has had a configured minimum time to work. A stop-loss, a take-profit and the carry rules shall remain immediate, because those are prices and economics rather than opinions.<br><br>A model's reversal shall additionally have to be CONVINCED: below a configured confidence it shall be reported but not acted on, since a small local model is not consistent between two calls minutes apart and acting on its hesitation costs two half-spreads. Where an opinion exists but may not yet be acted on, the window shall still show it — the minimum holding time is a fact about the trade, not a reason to hide what the model thinks.<br><br>Conviction shall only ever be compared with conviction from the SAME source: the composite's confidence at entry shall be recorded separately from whichever number decided the trade, because a model-led entry carries the model's own scale and comparing the two made every such trade appear to have faded the moment it opened.<br><br>The trading day's loud windows shall be treated as both opportunity and hazard rather than ignored, each measured on the clock it belongs to — the local exchange for the session edges, New York for the American releases and the central bank — so that the weeks in which Europe and the United States change their clocks on different days need no maintenance and cannot be got wrong by a fixed offset. The windows shall be: the first QUARTER HOUR after an open, which is fast, wide-spread and reverses often enough that it shall be sat out rather than merely sized down (it is also what forms the range whose break is the actual signal); the rest of that first hour, where the opening move becomes readable; the scheduled macro slots (08:30 and 10:00 New York, i.e. 14:30 and 16:00 in Berlin for most of the year); the central-bank window, the statement and the press conference that follows it, which shall likewise be sat out because its first move regularly reverses in full; the last hour before the American close and the final half hour within it. A scheduled release shall take precedence over the "rest of the opening hour" classification, being the more specific fact about that moment. Windows that are not sat out shall require more conviction to enter and shall be traded in smaller size, and both sit-out rules shall be switchable without removing the elevated bar. Leverage shall be bounded per correlation bucket on top of every other cap, with foreign exchange bounded tightest: a few tenths of a percent is a currency pair's whole day, so leverage that merely fits the risk budget can still place the stop inside the noise.<br><br>The session's own STRUCTURE shall be read and reported, because it is what a professional looks at before any oscillator and it costs no new data source: where the price sits against the first half hour's range (inside it, or broken up or down, with the excursion measured against the range's own width) and the relative strength of the technology future against the broad-market future — the cheapest available stand-in for market breadth, which would otherwise need per-constituent data this app does not fetch. Both reads shall be put in front of the model as evidence, and the bot shall refuse to open a position INTO a fresh opposite break of that range; where a series is too short for a read, the answer shall be "no read" rather than a fabricated one.<br><br>The local model's read shall be shown as a SOURCE wherever the app presents its evidence — in the per-instrument signals panel, in the decision window's source list, and as a hold/close column on the REAL open-trades table, where it is ADVICE: nothing there closes a real position, which stays a human action under REQ-N-005. Its side, its confidence and its own words shall be shown, and three states shall be told apart rather than conflated: "not configured", "shown this instrument and did not pick it", and "not among the instruments it was shown" — the last because the model can only speak about the candidates the prompt listed, and a reader who expects an opinion on every instrument is owed the reason there is none. The number of candidates put in front of the model shall therefore be a parameter of the prompt, and the consumer that reports a per-instrument read shall show it enough instruments to make that read meaningful.<br><br>Leverage shall never be a value the instrument does not offer: every ceiling — the account cap, the bucket cap, the instrument's own maximum — shall be applied BEFORE folding to the offered ladder, since clamping an already-folded value to a cap lands on a step nobody sells (an x8 ceiling on an instrument offering 1/2/5/20 must fold to x5). | T/A |
| REQ-F-035 | Prediction shall rest on AGREEMENT BETWEEN INDEPENDENT reads rather than on a stack of indicators derived from the same closes: an oscillator, a moving-average cross and a momentum study computed from one price series are one piece of evidence wearing three hats. The app shall therefore fetch and report reads that are independent of its own price history, each from a source it can actually obtain: the futures that lead the cash market (the Nasdaq future against the S&P future, i.e. whether technology is carrying the move or lagging it), expected volatility read by its DIRECTION rather than its level (the Nasdaq-specific index for a Nasdaq instrument, the broad one otherwise), the US 10-year yield whose rises press on growth shares, how many of the index's heavyweight constituents are actually participating, and where price sits against its own opening range.<br><br>For each read the app shall report the direction it supports, the number behind it, and — decisively — whether it could be MEASURED AT ALL. A read whose series is missing shall be UNKNOWN and shall never count as agreement: a confluence of "four conditions met" must mean four measured conditions rather than four absent feeds. Heavyweight participation shall be named as a STAND-IN for market breadth wherever it appears, because true breadth (the advance/decline line, up-volume, the share of constituents above their session average) needs per-constituent data this app does not fetch, and a stand-in presented as the real thing is worse than an honest gap.<br><br>The count of agreeing reads shall be shown per instrument alongside the app's other signals, shall be given to the model as evidence in those words, and shall gate the bot: an index position shall not be opened while fewer than a configured number of the MEASURED reads agree with its side. That threshold shall be configurable, shall be satisfiable (never more than the number of reads actually available), and shall be able to be switched off — with the reads still shown and still given to the model, because a read nobody acts on is still information a reader is owed. | T/A |

## Non-functional requirements

| ID | Requirement | Verify |
|----|-------------|--------|
| REQ-N-001 | The app shall build and run on Linux and Windows desktops with Qt ≥ 6.5, and shall be buildable for Android (APK via androiddeployqt, provisioned by setup.sh/setup.ps1 android and built by tools/build_android.{sh,ps1} for both arm64-v8a and x86_64, with the INTERNET permission the REST client needs) and iOS from the same CMake project. The Android APK shall be verified by building it; the emulator run is a manual step, since it needs a hypervisor the build machine may not expose.<br><br>Linux support shall cover ARM64 (aarch64) as well as x86-64, so the app runs on a Raspberry Pi 4/5 or Zero 2 W with a 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS Trixie (Debian 13) or newer — the OS floor is not a choice but a measured consequence: Qt's official aarch64 binaries require GLIBC_2.38 (libQt6Gui, libQt6Network; verified across Qt 6.8.3, 6.9.3 and 6.11.1), which Bookworm's glibc 2.36 does not provide, and Bookworm's own Qt 6.4.2 is below the Qt floor above. The host architecture shall be DERIVED, never assumed: setup.sh shall provision Qt's official Linux ARM64 kit (aqt host linux_arm64, arch linux_gcc_arm64, installed as ~/Qt/$QT_VERSION/gcc_arm64) and every Linux entry point shall resolve that kit itself (tools/common.sh), so no Raspberry Pi user has to pass QT_PREFIX by hand; where no ~/Qt kit exists for the architecture the build shall fall back to the distribution's Qt 6 rather than fail. tools/package_appimage.sh shall produce an aarch64 AppImage from the same script that produces the x86-64 one. A 32-bit ARM userland is explicitly out of scope: Qt publishes no desktop binaries for it and Raspberry Pi OS 32-bit ships Qt 6.4, below the floor above.<br><br>Pipeline stages whose tools exist only for x86-64 or only under a license — the Axivion analysis above all — shall report `skipped` on ARM64 with the reason named, never fail; and the stages that need a specific compiler version (MC/DC coverage, ThreadSanitizer: clang ≥ 18) shall resolve the version present on the host instead of hardcoding it, since a Debian or Raspberry Pi OS release ships exactly one clang. The ARM64 Linux build and test run shall be verified in CI on an ARM64 runner (the build-linux-arm64 job), because the reference development machine is x86-64. | A/I |
| REQ-N-002 | The domain layer shall be pure (Qt Core only, no I/O, no UI); layering (ui → services → domain) shall be enforced by the linker. | A/T |
| REQ-N-003 | REST access shall survive transient failures: idempotent GETs are retried on 429/5xx honouring Retry-After / RateLimit-Reset; non-GETs are never auto-retried. | T |
| REQ-N-004 | No secret (API key, user key) shall be stored in version control. | I/T |
| REQ-N-005 | Money-moving actions shall require explicit user confirmation (double-press) and shall never be triggered by advisory features (plans, watchdog, AI). | T/I |
| REQ-N-006 | Compute-heavy work (Monte-Carlo, trade-plan building) shall run off the GUI thread; the per-tick open-trades refresh shall be allocation-free (model/view, in-place dataChanged); the domain hot paths shall be covered by deterministic benchmarks (tst_benchmarks) and a profiling entry point (tools/profile.sh) with an optimized release build (./build_all.sh release) as the measuring target. | T/A |
